title: Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Amendment Bill 2021
short_title: Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Amendment Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change how the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor operates.
It would update the Monitor's focus on recently used laws, allow full-time appointment, and require reports to be tabled faster.
Reports would need to be tabled within 15 sitting days or 30 calendar days, whichever comes first.
changes: The bill would amend the Monitor's duty to prioritise legislation that has been applied or considered in the current or previous financial year.
It would let the Monitor be appointed as a full-time position.
It would require a new Monitor to be appointed as soon as practical after the role becomes vacant.
It would set a maximum tabling timeframe of 15 sitting days or 30 calendar days for Monitor reports.
It would mandate that anyone assisting the Monitor needs the Monitor's written agreement, which can be withdrawn at any time.
summary.affected: The Independent National Security Legislation Monitor and the Australian Parliament.

speeches.speaker: Ben Morton
speeches.brief: A motion was moved to suspend standing orders to give priority to three bills: the Biosecurity Amendment (Enhanced Risk Management) Bill 2021, the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Amendment Bill 2021, and the Crimes Amendment (Remissions of Sentences) Bill 2021. It also proposed that after the third reading of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Enhancing Superannuation Outcomes For Australians and Helping Australian Businesses Invest) Bill 2021, the House adjourn until 9:30 am on 2 December 2021, and that from 8 pm any divisions be deferred and a quorum count occur at that time.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Amendment Bill 2021, noting amendments negotiated with the Attorney-General that require reports to be tabled within 30 calendar days or 15 sitting days, ensure staff assignment requires the monitor’s agreement, allow full-time appointment, and clarify reporting and legal protections for staff, following recommendations by former ASIO director-general Dennis Richardson.

speeches.speaker: Ben Morton
speeches.brief: The bill implements recommendations from the 2019 Comprehensive Review to allow the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor to report on urgent matters beyond the annual report, with additional government amendments to ensure appropriate reporting and staffing arrangements for the monitor's oversight role.
